claims.text: The evidential base for this trip is unbroken, so the numbers the policy runs on are the platform's own. The GPS trace carries 45 fixes at a 10-second sample interval from 06:30:45 to 06:38:05, with 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, and both the trace and the trip record are assessed COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0. No limb of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is engaged — there is no gap above 90 seconds, no straight-line jump above 500 m, and no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds — so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes, no independent corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names is required, and no confidence discount under POL-GEN-02 attaches to the measurement relied on below.

The governing distance is the trace, not the receipt: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the measurement of actual distance and expressly bars trip_record.actual_distance_km, a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement, from the threshold test. The trace measures 3.96 km between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event against a booked optimal of 3.2 km, so the measured excess is 0.76 km, which is 23.75% of the optimal. The platform's own deviation derivation agrees: it records the excess at 0.76 km against a 3.2 km optimal.

On the percentage limb the rider's complaint is not an impression but a measurement: 0.76 km of extra driving is 23.75% of the 3.2 km planned route, above the 20% figure POL-RD-01 sets, and the rider's own words — 'a short hop became 3.96 km' — track the trace figure exactly. The rider's advocate is careful to claim this limb only; the clause requires both limbs to pass and does not treat the percentage figure as sufficient on its own.

The rider's advocate does not put this trip over the establishment gate, because the record does not support doing so. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH limbs to pass — the excess must be greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms — and the measured excess of 0.76 km falls 0.04 km short of the absolute limb, so the 23.75% figure above cannot carry the claim on its own and no deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip. Nor is the shortfall an artefact of which distance field is used: the rounded trip-record copy of 4.0 km yields exactly 0.80 km, which the clause's 'greater than 0.8 km' wording equally excludes. On the distance limb the rider is 0.04 km short, and that shortfall is the whole of the case on deviation.

The driver's only explanation on file — 'one-way streets' — is weightless, and the rider asks the tribunal so to record it. Under POL-RD-13 an asserted external traffic cause is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. No advisory covers the Jurong Point corridor in this window: EV-ADVIS-02843-01 is MISSING, carries weight_multiplier 0.0 and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the comparison POL-RD-03 requires cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The driver names no advisory id, so POL-RD-13(1) applies and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged: an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be an exculpatory clause invoked against one. The impaired artifact is cited here for its absence only — the rider discloses its MISSING status and 0.0 weight rather than resting any fact on it.

The driver's side of the POL-RD-08 burden is empty on every other exculpatory route as well. Once the rider has shown a common trip identity and a measured excess, the driver must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12; a general assertion that the roads run one way discharges nothing. Here the chat log contains zero messages, so POL-RD-04 has no rider instruction to run on; the trip record carries no pickup or dropoff amendment timestamp and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run; the fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not displace POL-RD-02; and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline is not in play and the booked optimal is not inflated by any pooled collection. The booked 3.2 km optimal therefore stands unchallenged as the baseline, and the measured excess is not reduced by any part of the driver's case.

The rider should not also be met with an extra corroboration burden the clause does not impose. The POL-RD-08 profile gate bites only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer, and then only for a claim whose excess is below 30%. On this rider's snapshot the trailing-60-day count is 1 and the substantiated count is 0, so the count limb of that gate is not met and no corroboration beyond the trace is demanded of this claim. Those two fields are named by POL-RD-08 and citable for it under POL-GEN-01; no other profile field on either party is relied on for this point. This does not reach the absolute-limb shortfall conceded above, but the rider asks that the burden framework be applied as written.

So that the money block is on the record, the rider states the arithmetic POL-RD-02 specifies and claims no more than it. POL-RD-02 runs on a METERED fare: charged_total is SGD 9.64; recomputed_fare is SGD 8.68, being (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 3.2 optimal km + 0.28 x 6.0 optimal min) multiplied by the surge_multiplier read from the fare_breakdown, which is 1.0, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus nil ERP and tolls, plus nil fixed surcharge, plus nil waiting-time fee, less nil promo discount; and the refund is SGD 0.96, which rounds up to a payable of SGD 1.00. That refund is not below the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is well under 90% of charged_total, so the rider would seek PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 1.00 and not the whole SGD 9.64. The rider contests SGD 2.00 and asks for no more than the policy's own figure.

claims.text: The governing distance measurement is the trace, and it defeats the claim. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field that governs the threshold test, and trip_record.actual_distance_km a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for it. The trace is 3.96 km and the booked optimal on EV-TRIP-02843 is 3.2 km, so the measured excess is 0.76 km - exactly what the trace's own derived block reports at derived.deviation.excess_km. That figure is below the 0.8 km absolute gate POL-RD-01 sets, and it is not greater than it.

Both limbs of POL-RD-01 must pass, and here only one does. The percentage limb is satisfied - derived.deviation.excess_pct is 23.75 against a 20.0 threshold - but the absolute limb is not, and because the establishment test is conjunctive the code-computed reading of this same trace is derived.deviation.status = 'no deviation'. POL-RD-01 then says in terms that if either establishment test fails, no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The rider's own claim text - '3.96 km' - is the very figure that fails the gate.

The result does not turn on which distance figure is used, because the absolute gate fails on both. The trace's 3.96 km yields 0.76 km of excess; even the trip record's rounded actual_distance_km of 4.0 km yields 0.80 km, and 0.80 is not greater than 0.8 km - the test is 'greater than', not 'at least'. POL-RD-01 also directs that the rounded copy may not be cited for this test at all. There is no arithmetic on this record under which the rider reaches the threshold.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. POL-RD-08(b) requires the rider to show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace; this trace is unimpaired on any view - 100.0% coverage, 45 fixes at the expected 10 second interval, no gaps and a 0.0 second max gap, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is not engaged - and it shows 0.76 km. The burden therefore never shifts to the driver, and the driver is not called on to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12 at all.

POL-RD-02 does not run, and with it every distance-and-time refund route for the rider closes. The clause applies only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01', and none is. The fare block's figures are therefore conditional, not owed: recomputed_fare 8.68 and refund_before_rounding 0.96 are what would apply if a deviation existed, and no deviation does. On EV-FARE-02843 the trip is METERED with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The charge of 9.64 is simply the rate card applied to the trip actually driven: 3.80 base fare, 3.00 distance (4.0 km at 0.75), 2.04 time (7.3 min at 0.28) and the 0.80 platform fee.

Pre-empting the smallest point available to the rider: the billed distance (distance_charged_km 4.0) exceeds the trace (3.96 km) by 0.04 km, about SGD 0.03 at the 0.75 per km rate. That is the rounding POL-RD-01 identifies between the trace and its convenience copy on the trip record, and it is not a billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4), whose subject-matter is unmatched gantry lines and misapplied surcharges - this fare breakdown carries zero ERP lines, zero tolls and zero surcharges, so that limb has nothing to correct.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be built against this driver. POL-RD-06 is engaged only by a MATERIAL deviation, and materiality requires an excess above 50.0% of optimal or above 8.0 km; the measured excess is 0.76 km and 23.75%, so the provision is not reached. Even if the profile were consulted, the only citable fields on EV-DPROF-02843 are deviation_flags_90d = 1 against completed_trips_90d = 228 - a ratio of 0.44%, below both the 3-flag test and the 5% test with at least 40 trips. Every other field on that profile (rating, lifetime_trips, prior_deviation_flags, acceptance_rate and the rest) is context only and may not ground any finding.

The driver's on-record note about one-way streets is not advanced as a defence and needs no supporting record. POL-RD-13 tests an external-cause assertion only against a traffic advisory for the trip, and the driver names no advisory and cites no evidence ID for one, so under POL-RD-13(1) the assertion cannot operate as an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact. The driver's case does not require it: the POL-RD-01 gate fails on this trip's own trace, which is where the finding must rest.

The outcome the evidence supports is NO_ACTION on this rider-filed dispute, and on a rider-filed dispute that is a driver win. POL-GEN-03 defines NO_ACTION party-relatively: the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands, with fare_breakdown.payment_status and fare_breakdown.refund_issued_sgd left as they are - here CHARGED and 0.00. The rider's contested 2.00 is not returned, the metered charge of 9.64 stays with the driver, and no escalation trigger fires because the deciding fact is carried by artifacts at full weight 1.0.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties, this is the ruling on trip TRP-02843.

WHAT THE GATE REQUIRES. POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace the governing distance measurement, not the receipt line: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 3.96 km (EV-GPS-02843) against a booked optimal of 3.2 km (EV-TRIP-02843), giving an excess of 0.76 km, or 23.75% of the planned route. The clause requires BOTH establishment tests to pass — the excess must be greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The percentage limb passes (23.75% > 20%). The absolute limb does not: 0.76 km is not greater than 0.8 km. The answer is the same on the trip record's rounded 4.0 km copy, which yields exactly 0.80 km, and 0.80 is not 'greater than 0.8' either; POL-RD-01 also bars that convenience copy from the test. POL-RD-01 states in terms that if either test fails, no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. Both advocates reached this conclusion and I accept it.

TRACE INTEGRITY. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c): 45 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 seconds. No independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) is required, and no POL-GEN-02 confidence discount attaches to the measurement.

THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. The counterparty note 'One-way streets' is not weighed for the driver. Under POL-RD-13 an external-cause assertion is tested only against a traffic advisory for the trip, and none covers this corridor: EV-ADVIS-02843-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver names no advisory evidence ID, POL-RD-13(1) applies — an assertion citing no artifact cannot be invoked against one — so this is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. The case does not need the driver's excuse: the claim fails on the rider's own measurement.

THE DRIVER'S OTHER ROUTES ARE EMPTY (accepted). The chat log EV-CHAT-02843 holds zero messages, so POL-RD-04 has no rider instruction to run on; the trip record has no pickup/dropoff amendment and both amended optimal fields are null, so POL-RD-05 cannot run; the fare model is METERED (EV-FARE-02843), so POL-RD-11 does not displace POL-RD-02; vehicle type is RYDE_X, so POL-RD-12's pooled baseline is not in play.

THE RIDER'S MONEY CLAIM (rejected). The POL-RD-02 arithmetic is right as arithmetic — charged_total SGD 9.64, recomputed_fare SGD 8.68 ((3.80 + 0.75 x 3.2 + 0.28 x 6.0) x 1.0 surge read from the fare breakdown + 0.80 platform fee), refund 0.96 rounding UP to a payable of SGD 1.00 — but POL-RD-02 runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01', and none is. The refund is conditional and is not payable. The rider's contested SGD 2.00 is not returned.

PROFILE POINTS. The rider is correct that the POL-RD-08 extra-corroboration gate does not bite (deviation_claims_60d 1, deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0); that is accepted, and it cannot help, because the gate could only have added a burden and the claim fails the threshold on its own. The driver is correct that no repeat-deviation pattern is engaged: POL-RD-06 is reached only by a MATERIAL deviation and 0.76 km / 23.75% is far below the 50% / 8.0 km line, and the only citable counters (deviation_flags_90d 1, completed_trips_90d 228) meet neither the 3-flag nor the 5% test. Every other profile field named in passing — rating, lifetime_trips, prior_deviation_flags, acceptance_rate — is context only under POL-GEN-01 and grounds nothing.

BILLING INTEGRITY. EV-FARE-02843 carries zero ERP lines, zero tolls and zero surcharges, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to correct, and no POL-RD-10(8) line exists. The billed 4.0 km against the trace's 3.96 km is the rounding difference POL-RD-01 describes, about SGD 0.03, not a phantom charge.

OUTCOME. NO_ACTION. The metered charge of SGD 9.64 stands; payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 are left as they are. The monetary effect is nil, below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, and no POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires, so no human review is required. The rider's claim is defeated by the absolute limb of the POL-RD-01 gate, carried by the trace and the trip record, both at weight_multiplier 1.0.

The burden therefore never shifts to the driver, and the driver is not called on to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12 at all.

POL-RD-02 does not run, and with it every distance-and-time refund route for the rider closes. The clause applies only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01', and none is. The fare block's figures are therefore conditional, not owed: recomputed_fare 8.68 and refund_before_rounding 0.96 are what would apply if a deviation existed, and no deviation does. On EV-FARE-02843 the trip is METERED with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The charge of 9.64 is simply the rate card applied to the trip actually driven: 3.80 base fare, 3.00 distance (4.0 km at 0.75), 2.04 time (7.3 min at 0.28) and the 0.80 platform fee.

Pre-empting the smallest point available to the rider: the billed distance (distance_charged_km 4.0) exceeds the trace (3.96 km) by 0.04 km, about SGD 0.03 at the 0.75 per km rate. That is the rounding POL-RD-01 identifies between the trace and its convenience copy on the trip record, and it is not a billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4), whose subject-matter is unmatched gantry lines and misapplied surcharges - this fare breakdown carries zero ERP lines, zero tolls and zero surcharges, so that limb has nothing to correct.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be built against this driver. POL-RD-06 is engaged only by a MATERIAL deviation, and materiality requires an excess above 50.0% of optimal or above 8.0 km; the measured excess is 0.76 km and 23.75%, so the provision is not reached. Even if the profile were consulted, the only citable fields on EV-DPROF-02843 are deviation_flags_90d = 1 against completed_trips_90d = 228 - a ratio of 0.44%, below both the 3-flag test and the 5% test with at least 40 trips. Every other field on that profile (rating, lifetime_trips, prior_deviation_flags, acceptance_rate and the rest) is context only and may not ground any finding.
